name: FDIC branch deposits × OT
label: FDIC branch deposits × OT: killed at burn-in (negative result)
verdict_html: The burn-in median next-year W₂² was 0.0078, below the half-sample noise floor of 0.0196 (ratio 0.399), and it was below the floor in every one of the 9 burn-in target years. By the pre-registered rule the object is killed: from one year to the next, the spread of branch deposits inside a state moved less than two random halves of the same state-year differ. The shape-only part of the move was also below its own noise floor. Separately, the planned test had power 0.07 with the 22 out-of-sample years available. Nothing was scored and no replacement object is proposed.
what_html: Each year, the spread of branch deposits inside each US state (FDIC Summary of Deposits): for each state and year, the equal-weighted distribution of ln(branch deposits) minus ln(the national median branch deposit), over branches other than main offices with positive deposits, in the 50 states and DC. Two optimal-transport methods were pre-registered against simple baselines: a pooled Wasserstein autoregression around the yearly barycenter, and a Wasserstein regression on state deposit growth. The plain-language explanation is on the learning page.
metrics: Burn-in target years with next-year below the floor
K3: shape term, next-year 0.0036937468 vs half-sample 0.0093507007
K2: shape share of the move 0.4200 (kill if < 0.15)
Planning power, primary test (5% gain, Holm 2.5%, T = 22)
rule_html: The half-sample distance is the noise floor: split a state's branches in one year at random into two halves and measure how far apart their quantile functions are. If consecutive years are closer than that, the year-to-year signal is below the noise and there is nothing for a forecast to beat. Any one of the pre-stated kill rules was enough; K1 and K3 both fired. Power is a second, independent reason not to proceed: with about 22 test years and a common year shock across states, a 5% gain would be detected about 7% of the time.
record_note_html: The design JSON keeps oos_authorized: false, and that flag is not the switch. Because the burn-in kill fired, an out-of-sample run of this object would not start even if an approval file were written later. A different object would need its own pre-registration.
card_desc_html:
Next-year change in the within-state spread of branch deposits was below the half-sample noise floor in all 9
        burn-in years (median W₂² 0.0078 vs 0.0196); planning power 0.07 with 22 test years. No out-of-sample run.
